sentences.text:
Author: K.Suresh Reddy
Bench: K.Suresh Reddy
 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice K.Suresh Reddy
 Criminal Petition No. 6886 Of 2023
Order:

The present criminal petition, under Section 438 Cr.P.C., is filed by the petitioners-accused Nos. 6 and 8 seeking their release on bail in the event of arrest in crime No. 38 of 2023 of C.C.S., Tirupathi,
registered for the offences punishable under Sections 406, 409 and 420 read with Section 34 IPC.

2. Heard Sri Maheswara Rao Kuncheam, learned counsel appearing for the petitioners-accused Nos.
6 and 8, and learned Special Assistant Public Prosecutor appearing for the respondent- State.
3.

Case of the prosecution is accused Nos. 1 and 2 are employed in Secure Value India Limited,
having its registered office at Resapuvanipalem, Near Athidi Grand Hotel, Visakhapatnam.
The manager of the said company gave a report on 01-08-2023 stating that accused Nos. 1 and 2 were allotted the work of filling cash in ATM Centers of various banks at various branches.
During verification, it came to light that accused Nos. 1 and 2, without filling cash in ATM Centers, have misappropriated an amount of Rs.2,51,39,300/-.
On the basis of the said report, the present crime has been registered against accused Nos. 1 and 2 initially.
During the course of investigation, the police arrested accused Nos. 1 and 2 and they were remanded to judicial custody.
Subsequently, by order dated 28-08-2023 in Criminal M.P.No. 1982 of 2023, accused Nos. 1 and 2 were enlarged on bail by the Court below.
Thereafter, by way of Memo dated 16-08-2023, accused Nos. 3 to 12 were added in the present crime stating that their involvement is also there.

Thereafter, the bail applications filed by accused Nos. 6 and 8 are dismissed by the Court below vide order dated 01-09-2023 in Criminal M.P.No. 176 of 2023 and order dated 01-09-2023 in Criminal M.P.No. 177 of 2023 respectively.

4. Learned counsel for the petitioners-accused Nos. 6 and 8 submits that admittedly, the petitioners have no role and nothing has been attributed against them; that the petitioner No. 1 is sister of accused No. 1 and petitioner No. 2 is wife of accused No. 2 and that the only allegation made against the petitioners is that accused Nos. 1 and 2 purchased certain gold articles and gave them to the petitioners and therefore requests this Court to grant anticipatory bail to the petitioners-accused nos. 6 and 8.
5.

Learned Special Assistant Public Prosecutor, on the other hand, vehemently opposed the criminal petition on the ground that during the course of investigation, accused Nos. 1 and 2 confessed that Smt S Sruthi vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/63186504/
1 they paid certain amounts to the petitioners and as such, the petitioners-accused Nos. 6 and 8 encouraged this type of activity by accused Nos. 1 and 2.

sentences.text: 6 . This Court perused the entire material available on record.

As the main allegations are made against accused Nos. 1 and 2 who misappropriated an amount of Rs.2,51,39,300/- and accused Nos.
1 and 2 were already granted bail, vide order dated 28-08-2023 in Criminal M.P.No. 1982 of 2023,
by the Court below, this Court is inclined to grant anticipatory bail to the petitioners- accused Nos. 6 and 8 with certain conditions.
7. The petitioners-accused Nos. 6 and 8 are, therefore, directed to surrender before the Station House Officer, C.C.S., Tirupathi, within a period of ten days from today.

On such surrender, the petitioners-accused Nos. 6 and 8 are ordered to be enlarged on bail on their executing each a personal bond for Rs.20,000/- with two sureties for the like sum each to the satisfaction of the Station House Officer, C.C.S., Tirupathi.
After release, the petitioners- accused Nos. 6 and 8 shall cooperate with the investigating agency and shall not tamper with the prosecution witnesses.
8. Accordingly, the criminal petition is allowed.
